nodes.name: African cherry
nodes.desc: A big montane forest tree whose fruit is eaten by monkeys, birds and other forest animals.

nodes.name: Cape pittosporum
nodes.desc: An evergreen forest tree whose fruit and foliage feed monkeys and many birds.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Forest figs fruit heavily and are a favourite food of chimpanzees, monkeys and turacos.

nodes.name: Herbs and vines
nodes.desc: Understory vines and herbs. Leaves, shoots and stems of such plants make up most of a gorilla's diet.

nodes.name: Lantana
nodes.desc: A shrub of forest edges and clearings. Monkeys eat its fruit and butterflies visit its flowers.

nodes.name: Mountain gorilla
nodes.desc: Mostly eats leaves, shoots, stems and pith, with some fruit. Bwindi holds almost half of all mountain gorillas.

nodes.name: Blue monkey
nodes.desc: A common forest monkey that eats fruit and leaves, including cherry and pittosporum fruit.

nodes.name: Mantled guereza
nodes.desc: A leaf-eating black-and-white monkey with a multi-chambered stomach for digesting tough plant matter.

nodes.name: African elephant
nodes.desc: Eats bark, leaves and fruit, and spreads seeds through its dung as it moves through the forest.

nodes.name: Great blue turaco
nodes.desc: A large forest bird that eats fruit, flowers and leaves, and spreads seeds in its droppings.

nodes.name: Black-fronted duiker
nodes.desc: A small forest antelope that mostly browses leaves and plant shoots, and also eats fruit.

nodes.name: Swallowtail butterflies
nodes.desc: Forest butterflies such as the flying handkerchief swallowtail. They feed on flowers like lantana.

nodes.name: Eastern chimpanzee
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats fruit, leaves and insects and also hunts monkeys. Bwindi chimpanzees were first counted in a 2025 census.

nodes.name: Kivu tree frog
nodes.desc: The most recorded amphibian near the park, a tree frog that feeds on small insects in the forest.

nodes.name: Johnston's chameleon
nodes.desc: A highland forest chameleon of the Albertine Rift that catches insects in the shrub layer.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: In rainforests leopards prey on duikers and primates. They have also been seen taking eastern gorillas near Kisoro.

nodes.name: Crowned eagle
nodes.desc: A powerful forest raptor that mainly hunts monkeys and duikers. It nests in tall trees.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Equatorial sun powers dense forest growth from the valleys to the high ridges.

nodes.name: Rain
nodes.desc: Roughly 1,400 to 1,900 mm falls each year, peaking around March to April and September to November.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Steep, wet Kigezi highland soils feed the forest, which in turn supplies streams to nearby lakes and farms.

nodes.name: Fungi and insects
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter, dung and dead wood and return nutrients to the soil.
